title: Screening Out the Needy: The Effects of SNAP Work Requirements
abstract: arXiv:2609.19660v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: We examine the effectiveness of work requirements as a screening device in the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP). Work requirements for "able-bodied adults without dependents" were suspended after the Great Recession and gradually reinstated across counties and states in the 2010s. Using linked administrative SNAP and employment data from five states and a triple-differences design, we find that work requirements reduce SNAP participation by seven percent without increasing labor supply and disproportionately screen out low-income individuals. We develop a welfare framework to interpret these results and find that the social costs of work requirements exceed budget savings.

translated_title: 筛除真正需要帮助的人：SNAP工作要求的影响
translated_abstract: 我们研究了工作要求作为筛选机制在补充营养援助计划（SNAP）中的有效性。针对“无受抚养人的健全成年人”的工作要求在全球金融危机后被暂停，并在2010年代逐步在美国各县和各州恢复实施。利用来自五个州的SNAP行政数据与就业数据的关联数据以及三重差分设计，我们发现工作要求使SNAP参与率降低了7%，但并未增加劳动供给，且不成比例地将低收入个体筛除。我们构建了一个福利分析框架来解释这些结果，并发现工作要求的社会成本超过了其带来的预算节省。
tldr: 该研究发现SNAP工作要求虽使参与率降低7%但并未增加劳动供给，反而主要筛除了低收入者，其社会成本超过了预算节省。
en_tdlr: SNAP work requirements reduce participation by 7% without increasing labor supply, disproportionately screen out low-income individuals, and their social costs exceed budget savings.
